finding: `_base_branch` claims to resolve `auto`, but `afk-config.py get` returns the raw value, and `auto` is the default. That is exactly the case the round-1 fix (r-004) was meant to refuse. The only new test of the real default uses an explicit branch name, never `auto`.

finding: The new read-back counts any remote tip that already contains HEAD as this step's own push. Because `_push` reads back before the first write (`read_first=True`), a diagnosis branch with no fix commit lands as done without pushing anything. Failing input: diagnosis branch at the old feature tip with no commit, and the feature branch moved on by one commit. land answered `{'status': 'done', 'how': 'found'}` and listed `push: feat/export@<old tip>`, so nothing shipped. Before this delta the same input answered not-fast-forward. Probe: a scratch pytest run on the test_ship fixtures.
why: ship.py:22-24 says land "check[s] the push is a fast-forward, and push[es] HEAD onto it". outside_writes.py:6 says a writing script records a write "straight after it succeeds". Here the entry records a push that never happened.
fix: Accept the contained-in answer only for a HEAD that carries a fix commit. Keep the Base commit that read_diagnosis drops (the `@commit` part of `## Base`) and refuse land when HEAD equals that commit or is an ancestor of it (`git merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD <base commit>` exits 0). Add a test for a diagnosis branch with no commit whose feature tip has moved.

finding: The catch-all turns every exception into `blocked`, with the text "a write may have taken effect, so re-run the step". That includes exceptions raised before any write. One case: `_base_branch`'s `subprocess.run(..., timeout=FORGE_TIMEOUT)` raises `TimeoutExpired` in land before the push, and nothing catches it there. The answer then claims a write may have happened and exits 2, not 1. A deterministic pre-write failure, such as a format-table ValueError from `load_format` in `_check_entry`, leaves a caller re-running a step that cannot succeed.
why: ship.py:35-37 says "refused (nothing written) ... blocked (a write may have taken effect: re-run the step, which reads back first)". The script's own pre-write lookup failure is mapped to refused at ship.py:340-341: `except Exception as error: raise refuse(f"cannot tell whether {branch} is protected: {error}")`.
fix: Treat a base-branch lookup failure in step_land the way `_guard_target` treats a protected lookup failure: catch the exception in `_base_branch` or around `tools.base_branch()` and raise `refuse`. Optionally, track whether a write was attempted, so the catch-all answers `refused` when none was.
